overview: Engineering and construction deliver one-off projects with long lead times, many parties and high consequences of error. Data lives in drawings, models, schedules and site records of uneven quality, and licensed engineers carry professional liability, so tools assist and verify and people sign.

concepts.name: Professional engineers are accountable for the design
concepts.explanation: Codes and law require a licensed engineer to design, check and seal critical work. Software supports calculations and checks, and responsibility cannot be handed to a tool.
concepts.whyItMatters: Any AI output used in design needs independent verification and a named signer.

concepts.name: Drawings and models carry the design information
concepts.explanation: Information sits in CAD drawings, PDFs and BIM models, often in different revisions and disciplines. Reading it reliably is a prerequisite for most automation.
concepts.whyItMatters: Using the wrong revision is a common and costly error.

concepts.name: Clashes between disciplines are common
concepts.explanation: Structure, services and architecture are modelled by different teams, and their elements collide. Not every clash needs action, and the important ones sit among thousands of minor ones.
concepts.whyItMatters: Prioritising by impact and construction timing makes coordination meetings useful.

concepts.name: Schedules slip for reasons that can be seen early
concepts.explanation: Delay comes from late design, supply, weather, access and productivity. Progress reports are often optimistic, so forecasts should use durations, float and risk drivers.
concepts.whyItMatters: A single completion date presented as certain misleads decisions.

concepts.name: Cost grows through change
concepts.explanation: Cost overruns come from scope change, design maturity, market prices and productivity. Early estimates carry wide uncertainty that narrows as design matures.
concepts.whyItMatters: Reporting a single number at an early stage hides the range.

concepts.name: Site safety is about conditions
concepts.explanation: Hazards such as open edges, exclusion zones and plant movement can be detected at scene level. Monitoring individual workers raises legal and trust issues.
concepts.whyItMatters: Safety tools support inspections and do not replace them.

concepts.name: Inspection finds defects before they are built in
concepts.explanation: Welds, concrete and structures are checked by qualified inspectors with measurements and images. Models can prioritise and highlight, but acceptance remains a human, certified decision.
concepts.whyItMatters: A missed severe defect costs far more than a recheck, so recall matters.

concepts.name: Contracts allocate risk
concepts.explanation: Contract terms decide who pays for delay, change and defects, and disputes depend on records kept at the time. Contemporaneous, linked records are the evidence.
concepts.whyItMatters: Missing records weaken a claim long after the work is done.
